correctness.rationale: The exact generator maps every subset product to proper-subset products with positive denominators. Induction fixes all \(2^{n+1}\) stationary moments, and Walsh inversion reconstructs every full-state probability. First- and second-order identities give the currents and cross-correlations; a stationary two-state transport equation yields the known equal-rate beta mixture. An independent full-master-equation rational checker passed 1,524 states across 21 parameter/size combinations, with a separate exact beta-moment check. Finite verification is supplementary to the proof.

The result claims no new classical telegraph beta distribution.

originality.rationale: Search and full-material comparisons support an original joint heterogeneous finite-star stationary hierarchy and sitewise heat-current decoupling relative to examined sources. Prior homogeneous-noisy-voter subfamily and classical beta-filter formulas are explicitly acknowledged as covered; the accepted claim does not repackage those alone. Historical priority remains provisional due to possible earlier Markov-modulated process equivalences.
residual_risks: Unindexed or older general Markov-modulated binary network theorems might implicitly contain this all-order subset recursion.
The published 2026 homogeneous star recursion covers a special common-noise subfamily; the new claim must remain restricted to its full heterogeneous-and-current classification.
The beta/PDMP limiting distribution is well established; no separate originality attaches to the beta limit.
The Cornu–Hilhorst 2017 full text was not read; only the abstract-level comparison is used.
No independent priority audit has been conducted.

value.rationale: The natural gap concerns reservoir-specific heat transport and complete correlations in a many-bath nonequilibrium network. The result is an all-size, arbitrary-heterogeneity exact stationary classification, proving a sharp and unexpected independence of each heat current from every other leaf despite strictly positive induced correlations. The finite star system is physical and parametrically extensive, not a selected numerical invariant; the familiar beta mixture supplies interpretation but not the basis for claimed novelty.
